text:
The week ended with the equity rally extending across the board. Bank Nifty jumped 5.64% to 61,034.1 and the broader Nifty 500 rose 2.19% to 23,734.2, while the India VIX fell 0.55% to 15.49, signalling lower volatility. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) kept buying for a 12th straight session, netting INR 47,093 crore, whereas Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold for the 10th session, net INR 30,161 crore. Breadth was “HEALTHY” with a score of 75.7; 81.8% of stocks stayed above their 20‑day average and 21 stocks made new 52‑week highs.

Recent IPOs showed mixed first‑day and subsequent performance. Bombay Coated & Special Steels listed on 5 Nov at ₹82, opening 11% above issue price but closing 1.1% lower; BLS Polymers opened 65.3% above ₹150 and closed 80.8% higher. SFC Environmental opened 7.6% above ₹330 and ended 45.6% up. M. K. Sons Fine Jewels and Jio Platforms both opened and closed in positive territory, up 5.6%/9.2% and 21.4%/25.2% respectively. No new IPOs are scheduled for the coming week.

Looking ahead, the market may react to domestic and global cues. A dip in Brent crude (down 1.60% to $96.75) and Gold (down 4.36% to $3,897) could ease inflation pressure, while the USD‑INR slipped 0.24% to 94.23, supporting liquidity. International equity futures are higher (S&P 500 up 3.02%, Nasdaq 100 up 4.59%), and the Nikkei rose 6.46%, suggesting positive risk sentiment. Key domestic drivers include upcoming WPI inflation data and any fresh FII buying, which has already infused over INR 84,000 crore this month.
